call_sites: imas_ambix/maps_cli.py:470 (`release`, the only command that writes the released version into the local bundle.json; AGENTS.md calls it at each landing that changed a bundle)

findings.text: follow-on: `_write_bundle_version` now creates its replacement with `tempfile.mkstemp`, whose file is mode 0600, and `os.replace` carries that mode onto `bundle.json`. The previous `bundle.write_text` preserved the descriptor's existing mode. Measured in a scratch copy at 1c7ffc73: a 0644 bundle.json becomes 0600 after the write. The staged copy uses `shutil.copy2`, so the mode would also reach the published artifact. Low risk for a gitignored local maps directory, but it is a real, reproducible behaviour change of the atomic rewrite.

follow-on: the landing fragment names the intermediate head `640ea2fc` (29 passed) and does not mention the stray-descriptor-temp guard, while the node's final head is `1c7ffc73` (30 passed). The manifest and the after_suite log carry the final head correctly, so the record reconciles against its own manifest; the fragment is simply one commit stale at commit time.

follow-on: the local write now happens after `push_tree` returns, so a failure inside `write_released_version` (rather than the push) leaves the registry holding a version the local descriptor does not name, until the next `pull`. This is the mirror of the defect the node repaired and is the lower-risk direction (an unpublished local version cannot be pulled by a facility), so it is a note rather than a defect.

Docked two for the mode side-effect of mkstemp (finding) and the global os.replace monkeypatch coupling the two release-path tests.
